inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,783 logical lines. The article develops two matched RH-conditional routes to the same sharp bound for S(t): an indirect route through an extremal bound for the antiderivative S1 and a local averaging inequality, and a direct route through odd Beurling-Selberg extremals. Its reusable depth lies in converting zero sums to bandlimited majorant/minorant problems, balancing approximation cost against prime-power support, and certifying the even and odd Gaussian-subordination measures. Formula extraction is generally recoverable from adjoining prose; only the two plotted figure bodies are defective in the text layer.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Differentiation exchanges even and odd zero-statistic kernels
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The passage from S1 to S is mirrored by passing from the even kernel f1 to its negative derivative f, explaining why indirect averaging and direct odd approximation encode closely related information.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source gives an analogy and matching result, not a general theorem that differentiation preserves extremal optimality.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: A three-way bandwidth tradeoff controls both proofs
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Exponential type simultaneously controls approximation error, Fourier support, and the size of the resulting prime-power sum; optimizing Delta balances these effects in both S1 and direct-S arguments.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The quantitative balance is RH-conditional and uses trivial prime-sum estimates specific to this explicit-formula implementation.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Local averaging and direct extremals reach the same pointwise constant
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The S1-increment route and the odd-extremal route produce the same leading S bound because one smooths in the height variable while the other bandlimits the corresponding differentiated zero kernel.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Equality of the achieved constant does not prove either method is globally optimal or that their errors coincide term by term.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Positive Gaussian mixtures transfer solved extremal problems to zeta kernels
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Both the even and odd kernels become tractable after representation by finite nonnegative Gaussian-subordination measures, allowing known unique extremals to be integrated and rescaled while retaining one-sided order and computable L1 cost.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The even and truncated-odd constructions invoke different external results and cannot be merged into a universal recipe from this source alone.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Measure admissibility is part of the mathematical mechanism
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: For the odd construction, the appendix's representation, positivity, and finite-mass proofs are not ancillary calculations: together they certify that Gaussian subordination is legally applicable.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: These certificates establish this particular measure only and do not supply a generic positivity test for other kernels.
